scope: 25 exact historical keys outside other assignments; historical operators and endpoint scopes compared with source and draft parent fields. The broad chronology of 3F2B was directly rechecked and corrected in a separate preserved qualification addendum.

rows.review_disposition: 3F2B can internalize Sieyès/Fouché containing the 1799 resurgence. Preserve the named mechanisms, minority parliamentary position and sequence, separately from earlier Directory repression phases.

Floréal continued manipulation of electoral choice after Fructidor but used distinct legislative scrutiny and purging mechanisms. Retire a loose continues edge only with this pattern in 29CD/F4D and the separate Fructidor event in 48B.

F4D’s analogy with 1793 includes renewed conscription; 7742 retains Jourdan’s actual age classes, compulsory mechanism and resistance. Preserve institutional novelty and later activation, not identical Year II institutions or a repeal claim unsupported by source.

677352/33CF must preserve constitutional royalists’ contrast with uncompromising restorationists. 1DB77 can supply only an explicit backward programme reference, not stand for every later restoration position.

381386 can internalize renewed émigré repression after Fructidor within the broader coercive campaign. Preserve departure deadlines, actual executions and distinct noble/priest measures without equating scale with Year II.

3F2B already spans 1795–1799 and can retain the February 1796 crackdown. Ensure clubs, theatre, purges and criminalization of 1793-constitution advocacy remain explicit and distinguish the tactical reversal from permanent eradication. The lead scope-qualification addendum corrects earlier overnarrow references to this parent.

Correct supported_by direction and preserve Mallet’s argument for accepting core revolutionary gains. It supports a limited-monarchy alternative, not proof that later electoral restoration was inevitable or directly produced by his writing.

60C460 can internalize abolition/war enabling black military power and the later attempt to restore slavery provoking renewed resistance. Preserve foreign expulsion, Toussaint’s autonomy, contingent Haiti and the distinction between Saint-Domingue and restoration elsewhere.

CB77 can retain post-Fructidor refusal to widen the electorate as continuity of the propertied foundation. Preserve renewed dependence on Jacobin activists alongside refusal, rather than suggesting an unchanged political alliance.

F4D can retain overconfidence after Floréal as a transition to costly foreign-policy choices. Do not make one year’s confidence cause all earlier Great Nation ideology or extraction; A4EB/2FE1/E37B retain broader phases separately.

F367 runs from Varennes to émigré concentration, whereas the old edge runs from organization to European alarm. These are not equivalent. Retire the weak intensifies-alarm formulation unless a precise source claim is retained; preserve actual organization, subsidies and monarchs’ conditional response in 2FF/621.

B888 can internalize the right-wing press supporting royalist electioneering and Clichy coordination. Preserve finance, persuasive attacks on economic failure/lawlessness and non-equivalence between anti-Directory readers and restoration supporters.

CB77 must retain Five Hundred initiative and Elders’ acceptance/rejection as a deliberate check responding to single-chamber experience. A component edge is unnecessary once these functions remain explicit.

43E040 can retain Granville linkage planning as a specific British intervention episode, while C4FA supplies broader self-interested policy. Retire the generic part_of edge without erasing slow preparation and failed contact.

CB77 must preserve the normative claim that property supplies independence, education and attachment to order. This is more than a technical qualification and belongs with the actual two-stage franchise.

Preserve constitutional separation versus later executive coercion as a design/practice contrast. Retire the broad edge only with CB77’s ministerial incompatibility and F4D/29CD’s subsequent subversion explicit; page 319 alone cannot establish the later events.

E268 can internalize conflicting United Irish, rural/Defender and French visions. Preserve organizational potency, shallow ideological unity, religious/social differences and Doyle’s conditional comparison with likely Dutch-style French supervision.

Correct the target: Boissy’s rejection of 1793 supported Year III design rather than opposing it. Preserve his judgment as attributed rhetoric and the actual constitutional contrast, not Doyle’s unqualified declaration that the unused constitution had no value.

304796/84FD/4F5D must preserve the concrete Pichegru–Condé–Lyonnais planning route and its failure to deliver an offensive. Retire a generic related edge only with named contacts and cautious chronology retained.

DFDC must preserve Toulon’s 1791 constitutional terms and hostility to old-regime social conduct as a limit on full restoration. Retire an extra contrast edge if that contrast remains explicit with 33CF; 1DB77’s 1789 programme is not an interchangeable restoration target.

The twin-threat framing helped justify government electioneering. Preserve this as the regime’s argument in F4D/3CBD and distinguish systematic intervention before Year V from later annulment; do not assert equal strength or purpose of Babeuf and Brottier.

677352 can internalize the pures/constitutional split, but the broader heterogeneity also includes popular rebels, courts, agents and foreign sponsors. Preserve those elsewhere in 7593/069F rather than silently reducing every division to one ideological binary.

AB9E/8EB must retain Calonne’s actual collaboration with Artois through money, administration and diplomacy. A generic collaborates edge can retire once the named functions and limits of foreign backing are explicit.

3F2B’s broad chronology can retain February 1796 closure and later military defeat, with 8B315’s Grenelle detail. Do not make earlier club closure a sufficient cause of later military destruction; preserve Police Legion and Grenelle mechanisms and temporary loss of insurrectionary capacity.

21A/F4D can internalize dependence on the army becoming vulnerability when it lost confidence. Preserve cumulative dependence and 340’s prospective synthesis, not a claim that reliance alone inevitably caused the eventual coup.
